\chapter{Sure and unsure}
\label{ch:ar-sure-and-unsure}
\hlchaptermodality{403}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say that someone made certain or grew suspicious, and say impossible, most probably and in general.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 403: I can say that someone made certain or grew suspicious, and say impossible, most probably and in general.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تيقن} (tayaqqana)}{تيقن (tayaqqana)}]{\ar{تيقن} (tayaqqana) — to make certain}

\label{lesson:AR-C403-tayaqqana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for not at all, then the Arabic for certainty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تيقن}}
\textbf{\ar{تيقن}} — \emph{tayaqqana} — \textquotedblleft{}to make certain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تيقن} \ar{الطبيب} \ar{من} \ar{سلامة} \ar{الطفل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tayaqqana aṭ-ṭabīb min salāmat aṭ-ṭifl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctor made certain that the child was safe.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتيقن}, \emph{yatayaqqan}.

It takes \ar{من}: \ar{تيقن} \ar{من} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تيقن}} (\emph{tayaqqana}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{y-q-n}, usually traced to the sense \textquotedblleft{}to be sure\textquotedblright{}. It is Form V, to make oneself sure: to make certain.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tayaqqana}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tayaqqana}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tayaqqana aṭ-ṭabīb min salāmat aṭ-ṭifl.} — The doctor made certain that the child was safe.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for not at all, then the Arabic for certainty, then say \emph{tayaqqana} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تيقن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To make certain\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ارتاب} (irtāba)}{ارتاب (irtāba)}]{\ar{ارتاب} (irtāba) — to be suspicious}

\label{lesson:AR-C403-irtaba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for certainty, then the Arabic for to make certain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ارتاب}}
\textbf{\ar{ارتاب}} — \emph{irtāba} — \textquotedblleft{}to be suspicious\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ارتاب} \ar{الحارس} \ar{في} \ar{الرجل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{irtāba al-ḥāris fī ar-rajul.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The guard grew suspicious of the man.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يرتاب}, \emph{yartāb}.

It takes \ar{في}: \ar{ارتاب} \ar{في} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ارتاب}} (\emph{irtāba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-y-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to disquiet, to raise doubt\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VIII, to be filled with disquiet: to doubt, to be suspicious.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{irtāba}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{irtāba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{irtāba al-ḥāris fī ar-rajul.} — The guard grew suspicious of the man.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for certainty, then the Arabic for to make certain, then say \emph{irtāba} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{ارتاب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To be suspicious\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مستحيل} (mustaḥīl)}{مستحيل (mustaḥīl)}]{\ar{مستحيل} (mustaḥīl) — impossible}

\label{lesson:AR-C403-mustahil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to make certain, then the Arabic for to be suspicious.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مستحيل}}
\textbf{\ar{مستحيل}} — \emph{mustaḥīl} — \textquotedblleft{}impossible\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{من} \ar{المستحيل} \ar{أن} \ar{ننهي} \ar{العمل} \ar{اليوم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{min al-mustaḥīl an nunhiya al-ʿamal al-yawm.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
It is impossible for us to finish the work today.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مستحيل}} (\emph{mustaḥīl}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-w-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to change, to turn\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Mustaḥīl} is the Form X active participle, what has turned away from being: impossible.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mustaḥīl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mustaḥīl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{min al-mustaḥīl an nunhiya al-ʿamal al-yawm.} — It is impossible for us to finish the work today.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to make certain, then the Arabic for to be suspicious, then say \emph{mustaḥīl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مستحيل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Impossible\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{على} \ar{الأرجح} (ʿalā al-arjaḥ)}{على الأرجح (ʿalā al-arjaḥ)}]{\ar{على} \ar{الأرجح} (ʿalā al-arjaḥ) — most probably}

\label{lesson:AR-C403-ala-al-arjah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to be suspicious, then the Arabic for impossible.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{على} \ar{الأرجح}}
\textbf{\ar{على} \ar{الأرجح}} — \emph{ʿalā al-arjaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}most probably\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سيصل} \ar{على} \ar{الأرجح} \ar{بعد} \ar{الظهر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sa-yaṣilu ʿalā al-arjaḥ baʿda aẓ-ẓuhr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He will most probably arrive in the afternoon.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{على} \ar{الأرجح}} (\emph{ʿalā al-arjaḥ}) joins \emph{ʿalā}, \textquotedblleft{}on\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{al-arjaḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}the weightier\textquotedblright{}, built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-j-ḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}to outweigh\textquotedblright{} (Lane): on the heavier side of the scale, most probably.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿalā al-arjaḥ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sa-yaṣilu ʿalā al-arjaḥ baʿda aẓ-ẓuhr.} — He will most probably arrive in the afternoon.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to be suspicious, then the Arabic for impossible, then say \emph{ʿalā al-arjaḥ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{على} \ar{الأرجح} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Most probably\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عموما} (ʿumūman)}{عموما (ʿumūman)}]{\ar{عموما} (ʿumūman) — in general}

\label{lesson:AR-C403-umuman}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for impossible, then the Arabic for most probably.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عموما}}
\textbf{\ar{عموما}} — \emph{ʿumūman} — \textquotedblleft{}in general\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{الطقس} \ar{عموما} \ar{جميل} \ar{هنا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aṭ-ṭaqs ʿumūman jamīl hunā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The weather here is generally pleasant.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عموما}} (\emph{ʿumūman}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-m-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to be general, to include all\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{ʿUmūman} is the verbal noun \emph{ʿumūm}, generality, with the adverb ending \emph{-an}: in general.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿumūman}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṭ-ṭaqs ʿumūman jamīl hunā.} — The weather here is generally pleasant.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for impossible, then the Arabic for most probably, then say \emph{ʿumūman} again
\end{itemize}
